finding: Despite its historical name/comment, the CSS assigns visual positions by semantic class/type selectors rather than direct-child numeric index: first p -> grid row1, last p -> row2, .af-sub-card -> right span rows1-2; mobile uses the same selectors to place p1 row1, p2 row2, card row3.

compatibility.desktop_after_order_fix: unchanged intended visual: p1+p2 left, card right spanning both rows
compatibility.mobile_after_order_fix: unchanged intended visual: p1 -> p2 -> card
compatibility.aside_to_article: safe for selectors because visual CSS targets .af-sub-card, not aside tag

implication: The physical stress-order one-shot fix and the aside->article role fix do not automatically require a new visual CSS package. Keep v003 as the visual candidate and simply re-run tight live source/target proof after structure changes.
live_required: desktop grid unchanged after any structural fix
